name: Jamiroquai
description:
'''Jamiroquai''' ({{IPAc-en|audio=Jamiroquai.ogg|dʒ|ə|ˈ|m|ɪr|ə|k|w|aɪ}} {{respell|jə|MIRR|ə|kwy}}) are an English [[acid jazz]] and [[funk]] band from London. Formed in 1992, they are fronted by vocalist [[Jay Kay]], and were prominent in the London-based funk and acid jazz movement of the 1990s. They built on their acid jazz sound in their early releases and later drew from [[Rock music|rock]], [[disco]], [[Electronic music|electronic]] and [[Latin music]] genres. Lyrically, the group have addressed [[Social justice|social]] and [[environmental justice]]. Kay has remained the only constant member through several line-up changes.

The band made their debut under [[Acid Jazz Records]] but subsequently found mainstream success under [[Sony Music|Sony]]. While under the label, three of their studio albums charted at number one on the [[UK Albums Chart]]—''[[Emergency on Planet Earth]]'' (1993), ''[[Synkronized]]'' (1999), and ''[[A Funk Odyssey]]'' (2001)—as did their compilation album ''[[High Times: Singles 1992–2006]]'' (2006), while their single "[[Deeper Underground]]" (1998) topped the [[UK Singles Chart]].

Jamiroquai were the third-best-selling UK act of the 1990s, after the [[Spice Girls]] and [[Oasis (band)|Oasis]].{{sfn|Larkin|2011|page=1987}} As of 2026, Jamiroquai have sold more than 26 million albums worldwide. Their third album, ''[[Travelling Without Moving]]'' (1996), received a [[Guinness World Record]] as the best-selling funk album in history. The music video for its second single, "[[Virtual Insanity]]",{{efn|group=nb|1="Do U Know Where You're Coming From" was technically issued first as a collaborative single with [[M-Beat]] in June 1996, making "Virtual Insanity" the album's lead solo single.}} also contributed to the band's success. The song was named [[MTV Video Music Award for Video of the Year|Video of the Year]] at the [[1997 MTV Video Music Awards]] and earned the band a [[Grammy Award]] at the [[40th Annual Grammy Awards]] in 1998.
